headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because aci has broad network egress and CRM/email access while MinerU can ingest documents via MCP and multi-threaded inference.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use MCP and direct function calls, and MinerU also exposes an MCP server. That shared bridge means content from MinerU outputs could be passed into aci as instructions if the orchestrator forwards it unfiltered. The profiles do not prove default trust, so this is an interaction risk rather than a guaranteed exploit.
conditions: IF the orchestrator forwards MinerU output into aci prompts or tool arguments without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF shared MCP messages are treated as instructions rather than data, attacker-controlled document text can steer aci.
mitigations: Add a strict data/instruction separator in the orchestrator.
Strip or escape prompt-like text before passing MinerU output to aci.
Require human review for any aci action triggered by document text.
Disable MCP bridging between the two agents unless needed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress. MinerU processes local PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text and can expose them through API/MCP surfaces. If the pair shares a workspace or documents are routed from MinerU into aci, sensitive content can leave the local boundary through aci's external integrations.
conditions: IF MinerU processes documents containing CRM, email, or support data and aci receives the extracted text, leakage occurs.
IF the two agents share a workspace or API pipeline, aci can transmit document-derived sensitive data to third-party services.
mitigations: Keep MinerU inputs separate from CRM/email datasets.
Block aci from receiving raw document text by default.
Route only redacted excerpts between agents.
Audit outbound destinations used by aci before enabling the pair.
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API-based actions, while MinerU supports multi-threaded concurrent inference but has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification capability. The overlap is mostly read/process plus external API use, so direct write-write conflict is limited unless an orchestrator maps both onto the same mutable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable CRM or document queue, race conditions can occur.
IF an orchestrator assigns shared OAuth-backed resources without locking, conflicting updates are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate queues or folders per agent.
Serialize writes to shared downstream systems.
Use optimistic concurrency checks on shared records.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same CRM objects.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document parser and aci can act on email, Slack, calendar, CRM, and sheets. If MinerU's extracted text is fed into aci without verification, aci may operationalize parsing errors into downstream actions. The profiles do not prove default automation, so the risk is real but not necessarily automatic.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction output is treated as authoritative input to aci, parsing mistakes can propagate.
IF aci is configured to send emails, update CRM records, or schedule calendar events from extracted text, errors cascade downstream.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before aci acts on MinerU output.
Require confidence thresholds for extracted fields.
Show source snippets alongside extracted values.
Limit aci to draft-only actions for document-derived tasks.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, customer support, and calendar data, while MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text. If regulated or region-bound documents are extracted by MinerU and then sent through aci's external integrations, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or customer support records are processed by MinerU and then forwarded through aci, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF aci's downstream services retain data longer than the source policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify documents before routing them to aci.
Block regulated data classes from cross-agent transfer.
Review retention settings on aci-connected services.
Keep region-bound data in a separate processing lane.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls.
